prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary (ideological language removed; no parties or individuals named)

- Investment and economy: Create a £400bn National Transformation Fund (including a £250bn Green Transformation Fund) and a National Investment Bank with £250bn lending over 10 years. Establish regional development banks and local transformation funds. Tighten rules on financial sector climate risk and London Stock Exchange listings.

- Climate, energy and industry: Target most emissions cuts by 2030; 90% of electricity and 50% of heat from low‑carbon sources by 2030. Build offshore/onshore wind and large-scale solar; retain new nuclear; expand tidal and hydrogen; permanently ban fracking. Retrofit almost all 27m homes to high efficiency; set zero‑carbon standard for new homes. Public ownership of energy networks and retail supply; windfall tax on oil firms; one million climate jobs; 3% of GDP on R&D; support green steel, gigafactories, plastics remanufacturing, and reshoring via procurement.

- Transport: Bring rail into public ownership; national electrification; complete HS2 to Scotland; deliver “Crossrail for the North”; expand rail freight. Enable municipal bus control with free travel for under‑25s where councils run services; restore 3,000 routes. End new petrol/diesel car sales by 2030; invest in EV charging and public sector fleet transition; increase cycling/walking funding.

- Environment and food: Climate and Environment Emergency Bill; new Clean Air Act; £5.6bn for flood defences; major tree planting; new protected areas and environmental tribunal. Producer responsibility for waste and bottle-return schemes. Right to Food, halve food bank use within a year and end need within three; net‑zero‑carbon food by 2040; reform fisheries quotas.

- Public services and tax: Reverse some corporation tax cuts; raise income tax on >£80k; no VAT rise; major anti‑avoidance drive. £150bn Social Transformation Fund for schools, hospitals, care homes and housing; presumption to insource; cap public-sector pay ratios at 20:1; above‑inflation pay rises starting with 5%.

- NHS and care: Average 4.3% annual health funding rise; end competitive tendering/privatisation; expand diagnostics and primary care; free prescriptions; annual free dental check‑ups; free hospital parking; net‑zero NHS. +£1.6bn/year for mental health, modernise facilities; expand children’s mental health. National Care Service with free personal care, improved workforce conditions, and a cap so no one pays over £100k for care.

- Education: Sure Start Plus; 30 hours free preschool for all 2–4‑year‑olds; extend maternity leave to 12 months; recruit ~150,000 early‑years staff. Increase school funding; class size cap of 30 in primary; scrap SATs; Arts Pupil Premium; local oversight of all schools. Free lifelong learning (Level 3 and six years at Levels 4–6); abolish tuition fees; restore maintenance grants; post‑qualification admissions.

- Work and rights: Real Living Wage of at least £10 for 16+; ban zero‑hours contracts; day‑one rights; single worker status; sectoral collective bargaining; stronger family and equality rights; reduce average full‑time week to 32 hours within a decade; new Workers’ Protection Agency; employee ownership funds up to 10% in large firms; pilot Universal Basic Income; cap exploitative overdraft/loan costs; tackle late payments.

- Housing: Build over 1m social homes in a decade (150k/year by end, incl. 100k council homes); end Right to Buy; redefine “affordable” to local incomes; new Decent Homes programme. Rent controls linked to inflation, open‑ended tenancies, national landlord licensing, renters’ unions; end no‑fault evictions. Fire safety fund and cladding replacement; end rough sleeping within five years with 8,000 additional homes.

- Migration and social security: End hostile environment and indefinite detention; close specific detention centres; family reunion protections; automatic rights for EU nationals; humane asylum routes. Scrap Universal Credit; immediate mitigations (end five‑week wait and sanctions, scrap benefit cap and two‑child limit, pay childcare upfront, split payments, fortnightly schedules); replace DWP with a Department for Social Security. Improve disability benefits; increase ESA and Carer’s Allowance.

- Pensions: Keep triple lock; keep State Pension Age at 66; review arduous occupations; protect pensioner benefits; transparent pensions dashboard; fairer auto‑enrolment; reform mineworkers’ pension surplus split.

- Policing, justice, fire: Recruit more police and rebuild neighbourhood policing; Royal Commission on substance misuse (harm‑reduction focus); restore legal aid; presumption against prison sentences under six months for non‑violent offences; reunify probation; stronger support for victims; recruit 5,000 firefighters; implement Grenfell findings.

- Democracy and devolution: Abolish the House of Lords, replace with an elected second chamber after a constitutional convention; votes at 16; automatic voter registration; repeal voter ID plans; decentralise and restore regional capacity; tighter lobbying, donations and transparency rules; restrict MPs’ second jobs; extend FOI.

- Digital, culture, media, sport: Free full‑fibre broadband nationwide by 2030 via public provision; digital rights duty of care. £1bn Cultural Capital Fund; Arts Pupil Premium; media plurality and governance reforms; support local media; football governance reforms and safe standing; modern gambling legislation.

- Brexit: Within six months, a public vote between a new deal (customs union, single market alignment, rights and standards guarantees, EU agencies participation, robust citizens’ rights) and remain; implement the result; no hard border in Ireland.

- Foreign policy and defence: War Powers Act; increase diplomatic capacity; human‑rights‑led arms export regime; climate diplomacy; support UN peacekeeping (£100m); NATO commitment; renew nuclear deterrent and pursue multilateral disarmament; spend at least 2% of GDP on defence; veterans’ support; UK-focused defence industrial strategy with greener MoD operations.
</text>
